records.title: MFLUX
records.summary: An MLX re-implementation of open image models for Macs. Each model gets its own CLI command (for example mflux-generate-z-image-turbo) and a Python class.
records.why_it_matters: It is the shortest documented path from a coding agent to a local image or upscale on Apple Silicon: one shell command per image, no server.
records.fit_notes: Install with uv tool install --upgrade mflux; an agent then calls the mflux-generate-* commands. First run downloads weights from Hugging Face, often 20-30 GB per model, and gated models (FLUX 3 Image Klein) need hf auth login first. The per-model READMEs carry the memory and timing tables; the top README has none. The GitHub repo moved from filipstrand/mflux to mflux-community/mflux. Nothing was run here.

related.note: GUI app for the same image models

claims.text: MFLUX runs image models locally on a Mac in MLX.
claims.quote: Run the latest state-of-the-art generative image models locally on your Mac in native MLX!

claims.text: Each model is written from scratch in MLX, with only tokenizers taken from Hugging Face Transformers.
claims.quote: All models are implemented from scratch in MLX, using only tokenizers from the

claims.text: The first run of a command downloads the model, which can take a long time.
claims.quote: The first time you run this, the model will automatically download which can take some time.

checked.what: mflux README (top level) against the three claims

records.title: mlx-video
records.summary: A Python package that runs LTX-2, LTX-2.3, Wan2.1 and Wan2.2 video models in MLX on a Mac, called as python -m mlx_video.<model>.generate.
records.why_it_matters: It is the documented MLX path for the two main open video families, with a command an agent can call and an MP4 as output.
records.fit_notes: Installs from git, not from a package index, so pin a commit. Wan weights must be converted first and conversion needs PyTorch; LTX weights have pre-converted copies on a contributor's Hugging Face account, not Lightricks'. The README states no memory figures and no timings, so check a short, low-resolution clip before a long one. LTX-2.5 is not in its model list as of 2026-11-12.

claims.text: It describes itself as a package for running and fine-tuning image, video and audio generation models on a Mac with MLX.
claims.quote: MLX-Video is the best package for inference and finetuning of Image-Video-Audio generation models on your Mac using MLX.

claims.text: It requires macOS on Apple Silicon.
Converting weights needs PyTorch installed as well.
claims.quote: For weight conversion: PyTorch (`pip install torch`)

checked.what: mlx-video README against the three claims

records.title: Draw Things
records.summary: A Mac and iOS app that runs open image and video models on Apple hardware, with its own release log of supported models.
records.why_it_matters: Its release log is the most up-to-date record of which open models run on a Mac at all, including LTX-2.3, MiniMax H3 and FLUX 3 Image Klein.
records.fit_notes: Best for a person to try a model by hand. For an agent the only interfaces named on this page are a gRPC server and in-app scripts; a stable CLI or HTTP API was not found here, so plan on mflux or mlx-video for scripted runs. The app has paid tiers and an optional cloud offload; their prices were not checked.

claims.text: The 2026-10-22 release added FLUX 3 Image Klein.
claims.quote: Add support for FLUX.3 [klein] 5.6B series models.

claims.text: The 2026-09-11 release added MiniMax H3, with LoRAs and TeaCache.
claims.quote: Add support for MiniMax H3 series models, including LoRAs and TeaCache.

claims.text: The app can run a gRPC server so another device can use its compute.
claims.quote: Add "Server Offload" feature which allows you to enable gRPC server on one instance of the app on a different device and connect to that device to use its compute.

checked.what: Draw Things downloads page (release log, visible text) against the three claims

records.title: ComfyUI
records.summary: A node-graph runtime for image and video models, with a local server. comfy-cli installs it and submits workflow JSON to it from the terminal.
records.why_it_matters: Many model vendors ship ComfyUI workflows first, and comfy-cli gives an agent a command to run them locally on a Mac.
records.fit_notes: On a Mac it runs on PyTorch MPS, and the README asks for a nightly PyTorch build. comfy-cli mixes local and paid paths: comfy setup also offers Comfy Cloud sign-in, comfy generate calls hosted partner models for credits, and comfy run --where cloud spends credits. Keep runs on --where local. The bundled default text-to-image graph needs an SD1.5 checkpoint that comfy-cli does not download. Which nodes work on MPS was not checked.

claims.text: ComfyUI documents an install on Apple Silicon Macs (M1 to M4).
claims.quote: You can install ComfyUI in Apple Mac silicon (M1, M2, M3 or M4) with any recent macOS version.
claims.locator: ComfyUI README.md, section Others > Apple Mac silicon

claims.text: comfy-cli runs workflows against a local ComfyUI server and converts UI-format JSON.
claims.quote: Run workflows against a local ComfyUI server, including auto-conversion of UI-format JSON

claims.text: Every comfy-cli command can emit structured JSON output for an agent.
claims.quote: Agent-friendly: every command emits structured `--json` envelopes

checked.what: ComfyUI README (Apple Mac silicon section) and comfy-cli README against the claims

records.title: whisper.cpp
records.summary: A C/C++ port of OpenAI's Whisper speech recognition, built as the whisper-cli binary, with Metal and Core ML support on Apple Silicon.
records.why_it_matters: It gives an agent a local transcript with timestamps for captions, on the Mac GPU, from one command.
records.fit_notes: It has to be built with cmake; the Core ML encoder needs Python, coremltools and Xcode to generate. whisper-cli reads 16-bit WAV only, so convert with ffmpeg first. Word-level timestamps are marked experimental in the README; for word-timed captions compare with the alignment in whisperX, which only runs on CPU on a Mac.

claims.text: On Apple Silicon the whole inference runs on the GPU through Metal.
claims.quote: On Apple Silicon, the inference runs fully on the GPU via Metal:

claims.text: The large model needs about 3.9 GB of memory and 2.9 GiB of disk.
On Apple Silicon the encoder can also run on the Neural Engine through Core ML.
claims.quote: On Apple Silicon devices, the Encoder inference can be executed on the Apple Neural Engine (ANE) via Core ML.

checked.what: whisper.cpp README against the three claims

records.title: mlx-whisper
records.summary: Whisper speech recognition in MLX from Apple's MLX examples, installed as the mlx-whisper package with a CLI and a Python function.
records.why_it_matters: It is the pip-installable way for an agent on a Mac to get a transcript file without compiling anything.
records.fit_notes: Needs ffmpeg. The default model is whisper-tiny, which is too weak for captions; pass --model with a larger mlx-community checkpoint. Memory and speed figures are not in the README. Output formats beyond txt were not checked.

claims.text: It runs Whisper speech recognition in MLX.
claims.quote: Speech recognition with Whisper in MLX.

claims.text: The CLI picks the output format with -f and the model with --model.
claims.quote: Use `-f` to specify the output format and `--model` to specify the model.

claims.text: Without --model it uses the tiny model.

checked.what: mlx-examples whisper README against the three claims
